instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a photo-sharing website. Users upload photos to an Amazon S3 bucket at sporadic times: some days bring a few photos, and some hours bring hundreds. Each photo needs a thumbnail, and creating one takes a few seconds. The company wants each thumbnail to be ready soon after its photo arrives. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Send each upload through a load balancer to an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances that create the thumbnails.

options.label: B
options.text: Run a container on AWS Fargate all day that polls the bucket for new photos and creates a thumbnail for each one.

options.label: C
options.text: Run a cron job on an Amazon EC2 instance that lists the bucket every minute and creates thumbnails for the new photos.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function, and create the thumbnail in the function for each new photo.

items.stem: A company runs an AWS Lambda function that compresses images that users upload. Monitoring shows that the function is CPU-bound: it uses little of its configured memory, but each invocation takes many seconds of computation. The company wants each invocation to finish faster and does not want to change the function code. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase the memory setting of the function so that Lambda allocates more CPU power to the function.

options.label: B
options.text: Raise the timeout of the function so that each invocation has more time to finish its compression work.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency for the function so that its execution environments stay initialized.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the memory setting, and choose a larger vCPU setting for the function in its configuration.

items.stem: A company runs a serverless order application on AWS Lambda in one AWS Region and keeps a standby copy in a second Region for disaster recovery. Last year, the company requested and received a higher Lambda concurrency quota in the primary Region. During a failover test, many requests to the functions in the standby Region fail with throttling errors. The company must ensure that the standby Region can carry the full production load. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Wait for a real failover, and let AWS raise the concurrency quota in the standby Region automatically when the throttling starts.

options.label: B
options.text: Request the same concurrency quota increase for the standby Region now, and add a check that compares the quotas of both Regions.

options.label: C
options.text: Make no change, because the quota increase in the primary Region also applies in the standby Region, and the throttling in the test was temporary.

options.label: D
options.text: Run the standby copy of the application on an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances instead of on Lambda functions.

items.stem: A company's order service calls an AWS Lambda function synchronously through the AWS SDK and does not use the function's response. Sometimes the function fails because a downstream inventory system is briefly unavailable, and those orders are lost. The company wants to decouple the order service from the function. The company must ensure that failed orders are retried and then kept for review, without changes to the inventory system. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the synchronous call, and configure a dead-letter queue on the function to keep the orders that fail every attempt.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the synchronous call, and rely on Lambda to retry each failed invocation automatically before it returns an error to the order service.

options.label: C
options.text: Invoke the function asynchronously, and configure an on-failure destination that sends the failed events to an Amazon SQS queue.

options.label: D
options.text: Add retry code with backoff to the order service, and write each order that still fails to a database table for review.

items.stem: A company runs an AWS Lambda function that writes payment records to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The database runs in private subnets of a VPC. The VPC also has public subnets with a route to an internet gateway. The function must also call a payment provider's API on the internet. The function is not connected to the VPC yet. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Connect the function to private subnets, and add a gateway VPC endpoint for the payment provider's API to their route table.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the function outside the VPC, and turn on public access for the database so that the function reaches both endpoints.

options.label: C
options.text: Connect the function to the public subnets of the VPC, so that the function reaches the payment API through the internet gateway.

options.label: D
options.text: Connect the function to private subnets whose route table sends internet-bound traffic to a NAT gateway in the VPC.

items.stem: A company runs an AWS Lambda function that answers product search requests. At the start of every invocation, the handler downloads the same 300 MB reference file from an Amazon S3 bucket, which makes each request slow. The file changes once a week. After a change, the company accepts that an execution environment keeps using the old copy for a few hours. Which combination of steps will make the requests faster with the LEAST development effort? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Store the reference file in an environment variable of the function, and read the variable at the start of each invocation.

options.label: B
options.text: Connect the function to a VPC, mount an Amazon EFS file system that holds the file, and read the file from the mount.

options.label: C
options.text: Cache the file in the /tmp directory, and download it again only when the file is not in /tmp yet.

options.label: D
options.text: Move the download out of the handler into the initialization code, so that warm invocations of an environment skip the download.

options.label: E
options.text: Have one scheduled invocation each week write the file to /tmp, so that every execution environment of the function reads that copy.

items.stem: A company exposes one AWS Lambda function to about 40 partner companies over HTTPS. Each partner must use its own key, and the company must restrict each partner to an agreed number of requests per day. The security team requires AWS WAF rules in front of the endpoint to block common web attacks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Put an Amazon API Gateway REST API in front of the function, with an API key and usage plan per partner and an AWS WAF web ACL.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer with the function as a target, an AWS WAF web ACL, and a listener rule for each partner's key.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a function URL with the NONE auth type, and check each partner's key and daily request count in the function code.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a function URL with the AWS_IAM auth type, and attach a usage plan for each partner and an AWS WAF web ACL to the function URL.

items.stem: A company runs a document-analysis service on AWS Lambda. A new version of the function needs machine learning libraries that are about 2 GB in size when unzipped. This is more than a .zip deployment package allows. The company wants to keep running the code as a Lambda function. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Upload the .zip deployment package to an Amazon S3 bucket first, and create the function from the package in that bucket.

options.label: B
options.text: Split the libraries across five Lambda layers, so that each layer stays below the size quota of one deployment package.

options.label: C
options.text: Install the libraries on an Amazon EC2 instance, and have the function forward each document to the instance for analysis.

options.label: D
options.text: Build the function and its libraries into a container image, and create the function from that container image.

options.label: E
options.text: Push the container image to an Amazon ECR repository in the same AWS Region as the function.

items.stem: A media company receives video files in an Amazon S3 bucket at unpredictable times, sometimes several files in one minute and sometimes none for hours. Each new file must be converted to a smaller format for mobile users. Each file takes about 30 seconds to process. The company has a small operations team. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule for new S3 objects that runs an Amazon ECS task on AWS Fargate for each file, and convert the file in the task.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function for each new file, and request a function timeout above 15 minutes in Service Quotas.

options.label: C
options.text: Run Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group with a minimum size of one, and have the instances check the bucket for new files every minute.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function for each new file, and convert the file inside the function before the function returns.

items.stem: A company runs workloads on Amazon EC2 instances, on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate, and on AWS Lambda. The total compute usage is steady-state and will stay at about the same level for the next 3 years. During that time, the company plans to move some workloads between these three compute services. The company wants a commitment discount for this usage. Which purchase option is the MOST cost-effective?

options.label: A
options.text: Buy three-year Standard Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances, and pay On-Demand rates for the Fargate and Lambda usage.

options.label: B
options.text: Buy a three-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan, and apply its discount to the EC2, Fargate and Lambda usage.

options.label: C
options.text: Buy a three-year Compute Savings Plan that commits to an hourly spend for the EC2, Fargate and Lambda usage together.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency on every Lambda function, and pay On-Demand rates for the EC2 and Fargate usage.

items.stem: A company runs a public API on Amazon API Gateway. The API invokes several AWS Lambda functions in one AWS Region. During monthly sales campaigns, traffic has sudden spikes, and some API calls fail with TooManyRequestsException errors. Amazon CloudWatch metrics show that the total concurrent executions of all functions in the Region reach the account quota at those times. The company must ensure that all requests are served during the next campaign. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency on every function for the campaign period, so that the functions get extra capacity above the account quota.

options.label: B
options.text: Request an increase of the Lambda concurrent executions quota for the Region in Service Quotas, sized for the campaign peak with headroom.

options.label: C
options.text: Move the API code to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer that scales on request count.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the current configuration, because Lambda scales every function on demand without a limit and the errors stop after the spikes.

items.stem: A company runs an order API on Amazon API Gateway. The API invokes an AWS Lambda function that writes each order to a small Amazon RDS for MySQL database. During traffic spikes, so many copies of the function connect at the same time that the database fails. The function must never run more than 50 copies at the same time. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency of 50 on a published alias of the function, and point the API Gateway integration at that alias.

options.label: B
options.text: Place an Amazon SQS queue between API Gateway and the function, and set the maximum concurrency of the event source mapping to 50.

options.label: C
options.text: Set the reserved concurrency of the function to 50, and keep the API Gateway integration pointed at the function as it is today.

options.label: D
options.text: Move the code into containers on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer, with an Amazon ECS service whose tasks keep running between requests.

items.stem: A company stores customer uploads in an Amazon S3 bucket. Amazon S3 invokes an AWS Lambda function for each new object. Some uploads are malformed, and the function fails on every attempt to process them. Today, these failed events are retried and then lost. The operations team must keep each failed event together with its error details and must receive each failed event as soon as possible after the first failure. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Add error handling code to the function that writes each failed event and its error message to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure an on-failure destination for asynchronous invocations of the function, and choose an Amazon SQS standard queue as the destination.

options.label: C
options.text: Set the maximum retry attempts in the asynchronous invocation configuration of the function to 0, so that a failed event is not retried.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure an Amazon SQS standard queue as the dead-letter queue of the function, and read the failed events from that queue.

options.label: E
options.text: Configure an on-failure destination for asynchronous invocations of the function, and choose an Amazon SNS FIFO topic as the destination.

items.stem: A media company receives video files in an Amazon S3 bucket at unpredictable times, sometimes several files in one minute and sometimes none for hours. Each new file must be converted to a smaller format for mobile users. Each file is long-running: it takes about 40 minutes to process. The company has a small operations team. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule for new S3 objects that runs an Amazon ECS task on AWS Fargate for each file, and convert the file in the task.

options.label: B
options.text: Run Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group with a minimum size of one, and have the instances check the bucket for new files every minute.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function for each new file, and request a function timeout above 15 minutes in Service Quotas.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function for each new file, and convert the file inside the function before the function returns.

items.stem: A company uses an Amazon SQS standard queue to decouple an order service from an AWS Lambda function. An event source mapping invokes the function with batches of messages. A few malformed messages make the function fail on every attempt. These messages return to the queue again and again and fill the function logs with errors. The company wants to keep the malformed messages for later analysis and stop the repeated processing. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure a dead-letter queue on the function, so that Lambda sends each message that fails every attempt to a second SQS queue.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure a redrive policy on the source queue that moves a message to an SQS dead-letter queue after a maxReceiveCount of 5.

options.label: C
options.text: Set the visibility timeout of the source queue lower than the function timeout, so that failed messages return to the queue sooner.

options.label: D
options.text: Add code to the function that copies each malformed message to an Amazon S3 bucket and then deletes the message from the queue.

items.stem: A company runs an order API on Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions. The functions write orders to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Each copy of a function opens its own database connection. During traffic spikes, the database returns too many connections errors, and some orders fail. Every request must be served, and the solution must require minimal code changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an Amazon RDS Proxy for the DB instance, and change the database endpoint in the configuration of the functions to the proxy endpoint.

options.label: B
options.text: Change the functions so that each invocation opens a new database connection at its start and closes the connection before it returns.

options.label: C
options.text: Set the reserved concurrency of the functions to 10, so that no more than 10 copies of the functions connect to the database at the same time.

options.label: D
options.text: Move the database to a larger DB instance class that accepts more connections, and keep the functions and their connection code as they are.

items.stem: A company runs an order API on Amazon API Gateway. The API invokes an AWS Lambda function that writes each order to a small Amazon RDS for MySQL database. After quiet periods, the first requests take several seconds because new execution environments start. Traffic never needs more than 50 copies of the function, and the API must respond with low latency to every request. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Place an Amazon SQS queue between API Gateway and the function, and set the maximum concurrency of the event source mapping to 50.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency of 50 on a published alias of the function, and point the API Gateway integration at that alias.

options.label: C
options.text: Move the code into containers on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer, with an Amazon ECS service whose tasks keep running between requests.

options.label: D
options.text: Set the reserved concurrency of the function to 50, and keep the API Gateway integration pointed at the function as it is today.

items.stem: A company runs a latency-sensitive API on Amazon API Gateway with an AWS Lambda function. To remove cold starts, a developer published a version of the function, created an alias named live that points to the version, and configured provisioned concurrency on the alias. However, users still see slow responses after quiet periods. The API Gateway integration invokes the function by its unqualified ARN. The API must respond with low latency. Which change will fix the problem with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency on the $LATEST version of the function, so that calls to the unqualified ARN use initialized environments.

options.label: B
options.text: Move the API code to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer, with instances that keep running.

options.label: C
options.text: Update the API Gateway integration so that it invokes the live alias of the function instead of the unqualified function ARN.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure reserved concurrency on the function equal to the provisioned concurrency, so that the function keeps its environments warm.

items.stem: A company runs a containerized web API for a mobile app on AWS Lambda. The API now receives a high, steady-state volume of requests all day, every day. Each request runs for about 1 second at a large memory setting, and the monthly Lambda bill grows with the request volume. The company wants to avoid managing servers. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the API on Lambda, and buy an EC2 Instance Savings Plan that matches the hourly compute spend of the function.

options.label: B
options.text: Run the API as containers on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer, with an Amazon ECS service that scales on request load.

options.label: C
options.text: Run the API on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer, and buy Reserved Instances for the instances.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the API on Lambda, and configure reserved concurrency for the function at the level of the daily peak so that no request is throttled.

items.stem: A company processes clickstream records from an Amazon Kinesis data stream with an AWS Lambda function. The event source mapping uses the default settings. However, one malformed record makes the function fail, and processing of that record's shard stops for days while the other shards continue. The company wants to keep failed records for later analysis and keep each shard moving. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Add code to the function that catches parse errors, writes each malformed record to an Amazon S3 bucket, and returns success for the batch.

options.label: B
options.text: On the event source mapping, turn on bisect batch on function error, set a retry limit, and add an Amazon SQS queue as the on-failure destination.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure a dead-letter queue on the function, so that Lambda moves the malformed record to an Amazon SQS queue after its retries end.

options.label: D
options.text: Raise the parallelization factor of the event source mapping, so that other concurrent batches from the same shard move past the malformed record.

items.stem: A company runs an order workflow as a chain of five AWS Lambda functions. Each function calls the next function synchronously with the AWS SDK and waits for its answer. Retry logic is written by hand in every function. Costs are higher than expected, and when an order fails, the team cannot see which step failed. The company wants to orchestrate the steps with managed retries and a clear view of each step. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Merge the five functions into one larger function that runs every step in order, and keep the retry code for each step inside it.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an AWS Step Functions state machine that runs each function as one task, with retry and error handling rules for each step.

options.label: C
options.text: Raise the timeout of each calling function, so that each caller waits longer for the next function and has time for its retries.

options.label: D
options.text: Put an Amazon SQS queue between each pair of functions, and build a dashboard from custom metrics that each function publishes about its step.

items.stem: A company runs many AWS Lambda functions in one AWS Region. Each night, a batch job invokes thousands of copies of one function at the same time and uses all of the concurrency that the account has in the Region. During the batch job, the mission-critical payment function is throttled. The company must ensure that the payment function can always scale to its usual peak of 200 concurrent executions. What should a solutions architect do?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure reserved concurrency of 200 for the payment function.

options.label: B
options.text: Change nothing, because each function scales on demand without a limit.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency for the batch function.

options.label: D
options.text: Increase the memory setting of the payment function.
